A321 Flight Attendant and Captain reported a fumes event during initial approach for landing.
show: 2023-07 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Initial Approach
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: A321 Ramp Agent reported being heavily overworked in exhausting work conditions due to staffing issues. Battery-powered wheelchairs being loaded into cargo without proper tagging and information also caused delays and safety issues due to the potential risk of fire from the lithium batteries in the cargo hold.
Maintenance Stock Clerk reported improperly shipping a HAZMAT item due to miscommunication and unfamiliarity with HAZMAT shipping and processing procedures.
PA-34 Seneca pilot reported electrical failure inflight prompting an immediate landing the nearest suitable airport.

PA-28-181 instructor pilot reported an engine loud bang during the initial climb in the pattern; from a Tower controlled airport; on a training flight. The instructor took control from the student and notified ATC and reduced power to reduce the engine banging noise; and immediately returned to land on the takeoff runway in the opposite direction. The aircraft landed safely; and was able to taxi clear of the runway.

King Air C90 pilot reported right engine loss of power resulting in controllability; performance and maneuverability issues in the landing pattern. The pilot stabilized the aircraft; secured the engine and landed safely.
Single pilot reported the loss of the GPS navigation system during landing approach. The pilot disengaged all related navigation systems and manually completed a safe landing for maintenance support.
GA pilot reported filing an IFR flight plan for a flight in IMC. The flight was completed as planned. The pilot realized later; the Obstacle Departure Procedure should have been flown as published.

Instructor pilot reported the student and instructor over corrected the controls when the tail wheel aircraft began to pull to left side of the runway. The over correction caused the aircraft to slide sideways and the left main folded under the aircraft. The wingtip made contact with the runway.
Flight Instructor reported an NMAC after receiving a late hand off by ATC while flying in congested airspace.
Instructor pilot reported executing an evasive maneuver due to an NMAC event with an erratically maneuvering aircraft. The instructor evaded close to the terrain which triggered a terrain warning.

Piper J-5A pilot reported a loss of control while landing in gusty wind conditions.  As the aircraft touched down; the pilot turned the aircraft into the wind; and over-correcting with the brakes resulted in the aircraft flipping onto its nose.
Single engine pilot reported not following IFR procedures while in IMC. The pilot states executing a missed approach and not informing ATC. The pilot did not follow the missed approach procedure.

SCT TRACON Controller reported they did not notice a VFR aircraft climb through the altitude of an aircraft in a holding pattern resulting in an NMAC. The reporter was working combined sectors due to staffing shortages and stated they were too busy to notice the confliction.

B737-800 Captain reported uncommanded aircraft movement during the push back; when the aircraft was released from the push back tractor there was no communication with the cockpit to set the parking brake.

B737 MAX 8 pilots reported after lift off a loud squeal developed on all communication systems. The crew was able to contact Dispatch through ACARS and get an ATC clearance to land at destination. The pilots communicated with the flight attendants verbally at the flight deck door. On the ground communications returned to normal.

B767 Captain reported a stick shaker while retracting the flaps on a departure procedure. The Captain indicated the crew elected to leave the flaps extended in the climb through 17;000 ft.; due to speed restriction on SID. The pilot flying started a turn and the aircraft began an unintended descent; at the same time flaps were retracted to a flaps 1 position. The combination of a turn; slower speed with flap retraction; and higher altitude resulted in a stick shaker. The PF accelerated the aircraft and resumed the climb.

Air carrier crew reported an altitude deviation and ATC low altitude alert while on approach to a foreign airport over terrain in moderate rain conditions. The pilot flying incorrectly determined and set a lower altitude than assigned from the approach chart while the pilot monitoring was distracted; and ATC alerted the crew of the deviation. The flight crew quickly corrected the altitude deviation and completed the approach and landing safely.

B737-800 Captain reported an air data computer failure causing erratic and conflicting readings of airspeed and altitude between the Captain and First Officer's flight instruments. The Captain determined via checklist that the failed instruments were on the Captain side and assigned flying duties to the FO. The FO maintained the flight manual pitch and attitude guidelines; validated airspeed and altitude with ATC; and diverted to a longer runway airport. The flight landed safely at the alternate airport.

A320 Captain reported 'no NOTOC' cancellation message received prior to pushback. After an extensive delay a message stating 'no DG cargo on board' was provided to the crew; enabling the flight to depart.

Air carrier Dispatcher reported a Captain was reporting the failure of a GPS unit prior to oceanic airspace. The Dispatcher had difficulty convincing the Captain that the aircraft was in a known area of GPS jamming.
Air carrier Captain reported a near miss with a UAS during final approach.
CE-560 Captain reported an AC electrical failure during climb. The flight crew diverted to an alternate airport.
Cessna 441 pilot reported a loss of power in one engine while in cruise. The engine eventually failed inflight. The pilot followed the QRH procedures and landed safely.

Student pilot reported while making a visual approach the tower controller gave the instruction to go-around; then changed to side step left then go-around; in an urgent tone. Later the student learned a pilot; who had lost communication; had been cleared to land via mobile phone.
A General Aviation CFI; on a training flight; reported the student pilot turned the wrong way at an intersection for takeoff.

TBM-940 pilot reported the aircraft lost airspeed and engine torque as the autothrottle began to reduce power. The pilot stated the throttle was attempting to prevent the engine from overheating after the anti-ice system was activated during climb.

Pilot reported being instructed to communicate with DAB tower through the frequency 118.1 instead of the published frequency 120.7 and that it is common local knowledge to routinely use the unpublished 118.1 frequency.
show: 2023-06 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred Unwanted Situation · Taxi
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred Unwanted Situation

text: Instructor pilot reported while in cruise the aircraft lost airspeed and the autopilot began to push the nose over in an attempt to regain airspeed. The instructor reported taking the controls from the student and pulling the autopilot circuit breaker. After diverting; maintenance found a large bug in the air intake vane.

Aerobatic aircraft pilot reported a critical ground conflict at a non towered airport. As the pilot was in the process of back taxiing and making radio reports to advise area traffic of position; a military aircraft made a low approach over the runway. The aerobatic pilot reported taking evasive action.
B737-700 flight crew reported an engine failure after takeoff; identified with a loud boom; resulting in a return to the departure airport with ATC assistance.
Air carrier stores personnel reported notification that a mislabeled 'non-hazmat' parcel was improperly shipped.
Air carrier First Officer reported a Hazmat parcel leaked in the DG can. The leakage was contained within the can and reported to Maintenance.
Air carrier Captain reported DG handling errors by ground personnel consisting of document errors; placement and tie down violations. Captain directed handlers to correct errors prior to pushback.
Pilot reported a NMAC while on final approach at F70 non towered airport during a training flight. Pilot performed a go-around and continued to landing.

Cirrus pilot reported receiving a low terrain alert from ATC during descent on top of a cloud deck near an obstacle on top of terrain. The pilot climbed as instructed by ATC and continued to destination.
Student pilot reported; while on a cross country flight; they bounced twice during landing. The pilot executed a go around and returned to departure airport and found the propeller was bent.
Cessna 150 Instructor conducting a training flight at a non towered airport reported a traffic conflict while on final approach to land with an aircraft taking off on a crossing runway.
Cessna 150 Flight Instructor reported a minor tail strike on landing on a training flight with a student after student failed to apply proper rudder inputs.
Sailplane pilot reported the canopy departed the aircraft during takeoff. The pilot contacted ATC; dropped the tether and returned to land.

PC-12 Captain reported a NMAC at an airport after the tower was closed. The slower aircraft was not communicating their intentions until final approach. The crew executed a 360 degree turn with the concurrence of ATC; then landed.
Home built experimental aircraft pilot reported a fire in the engine compartment after landing at a non towered airport. The pilot exited the runway and waited for help with fire extinguishers.
PA-23 pilot reported an unsafe gear warning. After a tower flyby the gear appeared down and locked. During the landing the nose wheel gear collapsed. The pilot reported minor damage.

S-76 EMS pilot reported after asking ATC to cross through their airspace on a medical mission; the controller asked the pilot to remain a mile north of the runway. Traversing the area; the EMS pilot needed to use evasive action to avoid an aircraft departing the runway.
Mooney pilot reported alternator failure at cruise. The pilot lowered the landing gear early and landed safely.

BOI Controller reported published altitude at IAF is below ATC Minimum Vectoring Altitude which resulted in issuing a low altitude alert to an aircraft on arrival. Controller reports this as a recurring problem.

TRACON Controller reported an aircraft deviated from departure procedure and entered an MVA. The reporter issued a low altitude alert and questioned the pilot's ability to maintain own terrain and obstruction clearance.
BNA Tower Controller reported not verifying an incorrect readback that stated a clearance below the MVA and was informed by the supervisor.
ZDC Center Controller reported an aircraft resumed clearance to PAAZZ after deviating for weather but ATC had cleared them to PAACK. The reporter stated the similar named fixes caused the confusion.

B767-300 Captain reported a strong burning odor and proceeded to investigate the source with a ramp agent. While the cause was undetermined; the aircraft was carrying items that were dangerous when wet and the departure conditions were rainy. However; inspection prior to departure was normal.

Air carrier Captain reported that incorrect flight ID information was being reported to ATC during flight. The aircraft transponder had incorrectly stored a previous flight number and transmitted it to the ATC system after it had been deleted and cleared.

Air carrier Captain reported rejecting the takeoff after receiving a GLD UNSAFE caution message and observing inaccurate radar altimeter indications. Maintenance replaced the radar altimeter sensor and the flight was re-dispatched.
Air carrier pilot reported a discrepancy between their charts and their navigation database regarding the distance between WURSOL and JINKAL on the RNAV Runway 14 approach to BUF.

CRJ-200 First Officer reported performing an incorrect sequence in transferring bleeds with an aircraft that had a list of MEL items that resulted in an unpressurized cabin without air conditioning. The cabin temperature became unsafe for the passengers and flight crew and the flight returned to the departure airport.

Small transport Captain reported encountering wake turbulence from the preceding aircraft upon takeoff. The passenger in the copilot seat then grabbed the yoke and attempted to perform dangerous maneuvers that would have worsened the condition. The Captain pushed the passenger's hands off the yoke and maintained positive control of the aircraft; and calmed the passenger.

CRJ-900 Flight Attendant reported during taxi that two separate passengers each had a bag that contained lithium ion batteries; and both were checked baggage. The flight crew then returned to the gate to remove the bags; the passengers; and refuel.

Air carrier maintenance team reported oxygen generators that had been misinstalled in the cabin were reinstalled by other technicians using improper procedures. Several generators were damaged and left unsecured on the aircraft.

Pilot reported difficulty discerning whether the runway at a nontowered airport was closed due to a lack of a prominently painted X on the runway. After landing on the runway; the pilot was informed the runway was closed for an airport lighting project.
Cessna 182 pilot reported a NMAC event while taxing into position and hold. The conflict was caused by ATC utilizing misleading phraseology in their instructions.

C550 Captain reported experiencing a sharp bump on approach that resulted in the autopilot failing and loose objects being knocked down. There were no injuries to the passenger and flight crew; but there was minor damage to the aircraft's lavatory tank.
show: 2023-07 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Initial Approach

text: Flight Instructor reported an NMAC event during landing training with a landing aircraft for a conflicting runway. Both aircraft made visual contact and both executed an evasive maneuver to avoid a collision.
Diamond DA20 student pilot and instructor reported that while the student was landing on their solo flight they bounced the aircraft twice; resulting in a propeller strike.

PA-24 pilot reported having trouble landing and multiple go-around attempts due to shuddering. On the third attempt and upon finally landing; the pilot shut down the aircraft and saw that the wheel hub of the nose gear had broke and a prop strike had occurred.
PA-28 pilot reported loss of RPM's during a touch and go and made a full stop landing instead.
First Officer reported failure to change oxygen tank resulted in confusing communications efforts with ZMA ARTCC and expeditious descent.
PC12 Captain reported smoke from failed EFIS resulted in expeditious descent and divert. Captain stated that mask required hindered ability to breath and communications with ATC.
show: 2023-06 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Cruise
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Small aircraft flight crews reported miscommunication of departure instructions resulting an NMAC event requiring evasive action.
C208 Captain reported effort to extinguish smoke and flame in engine compartment per checklist; resulted in engine over-temp and airport rescue and firefighting action.
Pilot reported strap or harness caused loss of canopy resulted in return to departure airport.
Corporate First Officer reported a loss of pressurization during cruise. Crew performed a rapid descent and continued to landing.
show: 2023-06 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Cruise

text: C172 Flight Instructor reported an NMAC while in the traffic pattern on a training flight at a non-towered airport in visual conditions. The instructor visually acquired the other aircraft and took evasive action to avoid a collision. After passing the aircraft; the flight instructor returned to the traffic pattern and landed.

C340A Maintenance Technician reported a repair to the vacuum pump and the following engine test run was incorrectly completed. The pilot flew the aircraft after the first repair and oil began to stream from the cowling and the pressure fluctuated; which led to the discovery of the problem.
Barron 55 pilot reported the aircraft began uncommanded climbs and descents after entering IMC in an area of turbulence and precipitation. Pilot exited conditions and continued to destination in VMC.
show: 2023-07 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Cruise

text: Baron 55 pilot reported the autopilot disengaged on final approach resulting in a descent below IFR altitude and a low altitude warning issued by ATC. Pilot climbed back to correct altitude and continued the approach.
Air carrier flight crew reported the number one engine failure during initial climb. Flight crew returned to departure airport and landed.

Air carrier Captain reported a severe jolt of turbulence during cruise which resulted in a Mach limit exceedance and an altitude excursion.The Captain executed the upset recovery with no injuries or damage.
Ground vehicle driver reported a ground conflict with an aircraft that was on push back requiring evasive action.
Dispatcher reported a flight over Central Asia experienced possible GPS jamming causing them to divert.
Aircraft maintenance technicians reported performing maintenance procedure improperly resulted in damaged engine cowling.
Cessna 172 pilot reported a NMAC in the pattern with an aircraft entering a crosswind for the runway they had just departed.
Glider pilot reported another aircraft on climb out from crossing runway passed below; resulted in taking evasive action and a NMAC event.
Local Controller reported witnessing an aircraft going off the runway during the rollout and saw it go into the grass. The pilot did not need assistance and proceeded to exit normally on the taxiway.

Tower Controller reported a single engine aircraft landed with landing gear failure following two other incidents. Controller reported facility non compliance resulted in fatigue and working beyond legal maximum hours.
show: 2023-07 · Ground: Gear Up Landing · Final Approach

text: B777 flight crew reported releasing the parking brakes before receiving and sending the final dangerous goods report.
A319 Captain reported having to brake hard to avoid a collision with a ground vehicle that drove directly in front of the aircraft while pulling into ramp.
B777 Captain reported experiencing wake turbulence and deviating from assigned airspeed to mitigate the effects and maintain a stable approach without informing ATC of intentions.
show: 2023-07 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Final Approach

text: B737 flight crew reported releasing the parking brakes and pushing back from the gate before receiving and acknowledging the final dangerous goods report. The flight crew continued the pushback and received and acknowledged the report afterwards.

B737 NG Captain reported they received intermittent SPD LIM and AUTO SLAT FAIL warnings at cruise altitude.  The warnings became steady and soon after the crew experienced a stick shaker and an over speed indication displayed on the Captain's side.  The flight crew decided to divert to the nearest suitable airport.
B737 Captain reported a vibration while accelerating and climbing to FL310. Captain diverted and landed safely.
B787 crew reported aircraft damage (hail and or lightning strike) that was detected post-flight after penetrating a thunderstorm while on descent for landing.

B737 Captain reported receiving conflicting information from multiple departments regarding whether dangerous goods were loaded on board prior to departure. After extensive delay and a lot of back-and-forth; it was finally determined that no DG had been loaded on board and the flight took off.

B757 Captain reported receiving a warning message at brake release to complete the DG acknowledgement procedures. After verifying that DG had been loaded; the acknowledgement message was sent and the proper response was received.

EMB-145 crew reported an EGPWS event during flap retraction on an autopilot missed approach after conducting an ILS approach to minimums. Crew took manual control of aircraft and diverted due to fuel considerations and weather at destination.

Cessna Stationair pilot reported an alternator failure and subsequent loss of all electrical power and battery during cruise. Pilot continued to destination airport using portable backup communication and navigation devices.

PA-46 pilot reported a runway excursion upon landing occurred when the rudder pedals did not respond to input. Pilot stated that during landings prior to the event the aircraft's brake and rudder system appeared to not be functioning normally and questioned if maintenance had been properly done.

Navion pilot reported landing on the runway gear up and was assisted by airport personnel in tugging the aircraft to the hangar. It was a hot day and the pilot reported not following the checklist procedures properly; and did not confirm the landing gear was down and locked.

C172 pilot reported being notified of another aircraft also on base that almost went unnoticed during a final approach at a non-towered airport. The two aircraft increased separation and the reporter proceeded to land.

PA-28 Flight Instructor reported a loss of control during landing as the Student Pilot relinquished the flight controls after encountering a strong crosswind gust and pushed the aircraft off centerline. The reporter performed a go-around and diverted to another airport where a ground observer could assess the status of the landing gear and subsequently performed a normal landing. Upon landing; the aircraft was found to be damaged in several places.

Small aircraft pilot reported inadvertently entering Class C airspace just after takeoff while maneuvering to avoid collision with another aircraft that was entering the VFR traffic pattern at a nearby airport.
show: 2023-07 · Airspace Violation All Types · Initial Climb

text: Small aircraft pilot reported while holding short at a taxiway; another aircraft came extremely close in proximity as it was taxiing. The other aircraft was taxiing at a fast speed and the reporter had to quickly stop while over the runway hold-short markings to avoid a collision.
RV-6A pilot reported an aircraft electrical failure while performing a final approach in VFR. The pilot landed without communication and taxied into a non-movement area.
TRACON Controller reported an aircraft made a wrong turn resulted in entering a higher MVA. The controller issued a climb to the aircraft.
show: 2023-07 · Airspace Violation All Types · Final Approach

text: Controller reported vectoring an aircraft during approach such that the aircraft's rate of turn resulted in them entering an area with an MVA higher than their assigned altitude.

B737 MAX 8 flight crew reported while preparing for approach; the aircraft alerting system displayed a reliability issue with the Captain's PFD and a Stab Out of Trim warning. The flight crew continued to landing at destination airport.
show: 2023-07 · Procedural: Weight And Balance · Final Approach

text: Air carrier Captain reported the runway markings at RCSS airport are worn and difficult to see; posing a safety hazard to landing aircraft in all weather conditions.
show: 2023-07 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred Unwanted Situation · Landing
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred Unwanted Situation

text: A320 pilot reported a low speed rejected takeoff after the loss of the yellow system hydraulic quantity.
Air carrier flight crew reported a hard landing during a training flight resulted when the trainee released back pressure during the round out. A passenger reported a sore back due to the impact.

Air carrier flight crew reported a mechanical problem with the spoiler system during a visual approach at night over unfamiliar terrain. While maneuvering on the approach; the crew received an aircraft terrain warning and executed a missed approach.
CRJ flight crew reported a hard landing when the trainee First Officer reduced power too early during the landing maneuver.
show: 2023-07 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Landing

text: CRJ-900 air carrier crew reported a terrain obstacle alert on a visual approach at night when they descended to FAF altitude on a non-published portion of the approach. The flight crew climbed to correct altitude and continued the approach to a landing.
Air carrier Captain reported recovering from an upset related to a wake turbulence encounter on approach to CLT in trail of a heavy jet.
show: 2023-07 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Initial Approach

text: Pilot reported receiving a No Takeoff annunciation from the aircraft resulting in a rejected takeoff.  Pilot stated they had received several false TCAS advisories during taxi-out.  Possible 5G interference was referenced by the pilot as a contributing factor.

Maintenance personal performing a routine check on an arrival aircraft found the alternate slat-drive unit circuit breaker pulled and collared. The unit was inoperable and there were no previous write ups in the last ninety days.

B737 Technician reported that an EA (Engineering Authorization) does not have a sufficient fuel nozzle leak check process after fuel nozzle post-replacement work is completed. If the leak test is not performed and a potential problem goes undetected; the reporter states that it can lead to in-service engine fires.
show: 2023-07 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Parked
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Pilot reported an inadvertent taxiway incursion at CXY airport after attempting to reposition an aircraft away from an uneven ramp area. After towing the aircraft to a level area; it was discovered that the aircraft was sitting on an active taxiway where a blind spot exists from the ATC tower's perspective.
Cessna 172 pilot reported encountering wake turbulence on approach to BFI in trail of a preceding jet aircraft.
Premier 1 Captain reported a cabin altitude warning after leveling off during climb due to an excessive cabin altitude rate of climb.  Aircraft returned to departure airport for maintenance.
Citation Excel pilot reported an ACC DOOR UNLOCKED warning after takeoff and returned to departure airport as a precaution.

GA pilot reported an NMAC while on climbout from GYI airport requiring evasive action to avoid a collision.  Reporter stated the conflicting aircraft was not communicating with Tower and probably never saw their aircraft.
Center Controller reported an IFR aircraft descended from their assigned altitude and changed to advisory frequency without a clearance and descended below the Minimum IFR Altitude.
A320 Captain reported Ground Personnel disconnect the tug from aircraft without coordination with crew resulting in aircraft movement and vibration.
show: 2023-07 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Parked

text: B737 NG flight crew reported they failed to get the Final DG Summary prior to brake release. The flight crew requested and received the Final DG Summary and notified Dispatch prior to pushback.

Air Carrier Ramp Personnel reported a safety concern regarding checked passenger bags with USB ports which could possibly be powered during transit. Powered batteries in cargo create a serious thermal runaway hazard.
show: 2023-07 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred Unwanted Situation · Parked
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred Unwanted Situation

text: B737-800 First Officer reported a high speed abort was executed due to a miscommunication of multiple parts of the ground operation regarding a DG document.

Air carrier Captain reported cabin odor and walls in the aft lavatory were extremely hot; as reported by the aft Flight Attendant. After a divert; a missed approach due to arriving too high on final and then an overweight landing; the aircraft arrived safely. The Fire Marshal and maintenance determined the aft water heater was running uncontrolled full power and overheating.

Flight instructor reported an NMAC during climb after a short approach with an aircraft executing an instrument approach to an intersecting and virtually opposite direction runway.  Flight instructor had student level off below pattern altitude to avoid a collision.

Instructor pilot reported a NMAC while in the traffic pattern at a towered airport. The offending twin engine aircraft was practicing an engine out approach and drifted off course. The twin passed overhead of the instructor's aircraft.

Instructor pilot; with another instructor; reported a NMAC at a non-towered airport. The instructor states they were cut of; while on final approach; by a non communicating aircraft. An immediate climb was required to avoid a collision as reported by the instructor.
A TRACON Controller reported they descended an aircraft to an altitude below the Minimum Vectoring Altitude.
A319 Captain reported being summoned to return to departure gate to correct a DG loading discrepancy before departing.
Air Carrier Storekeeper reported being questioned about shipping an explosive component. Storekeeper denied recalling any knowledge of that occurring.
show: 2023-02 · No Specific Anomaly Occurred Unwanted Situation · Unknown
cat: No Specific Anomaly Occurred Unwanted Situation

text: Air carrier Ground Personnel reported being notified of a box containing two Dangerous Goods (DG) components combined in one box. Reporter stated he was not aware of any DG in the box.

EMB-175 flight crew reported receiving a FLAP FAIL EICAS message during climbout.  The flaps were reportedly stuck at position 1 while the slats were stuck at position 3.  The crew decided to divert to the nearest suitable airport after not being able to resolve the issue.

B747-400 pilot reported an unsuccessful auto land in VMC conditions at a Tower controlled airport. The air carrier crew missed briefing a note on the approach plate prohibiting auto coupled approaches to the intended landing runway. The PF (pilot flying) disconnected the Autopilot in the flare due to erratic inputs and landed manually.
A321 Captain reported abnormal bleed air pressure on left engine during climb. Captain returned to departure airport due to icing restrictions and made an overweight landing.
B737-800 Captain reported executing a rejected takeoff due to airspeed disagree message on primary flight display. Captain returned to gate for maintenance and brake cooling.

B777-200 Captain reported Hazmat final documents missing details of a Hazmat apparatus that was loaded on broad. After an intensive attempt to obtain details of the item were located the Captain had the apparatus removed.
B737-800 crew reported a blown tire during takeoff. Crew continued on to destination and landed uneventfully.

B767-300 First Officer reported experiencing a momentary stick shaker after a wake turbulence encounter departing PHX on the FORPE1 SID in trail of another jet transport. Reporter cited the design of the departure procedure as contributing.
EMB-145 First Officer reported encountering wake turbulence departing CLT in trail of an Airbus. Reporter suggested increased spacing on departures.
show: 2023-07 · Inflight: Wake Vortex Encounter · Initial Climb

text: Pilot reported reoccurring difficulties in communicating with ZMP ARTCC via multiple frequencies in the vicinity of MBL airport.
Air carrier Flight Attendant reported the seal of a Lithium Ion battery bag was broken.
Air carrier ground personnel reported being notified that the load document was incorrect and caused a flight delay to correct.

C750 pilot reported descending below the minimum altitude depicted on a descend via STAR because of an improperly set altitude pre-select value. Crew queried ATC and were given a heading and altitude for terrain avoidance and landed normally.
show: 2023-07 · Altitude: Crossing Restriction Not Met · Initial Approach

text: Rotorcraft pilot reported during liftoff; they passed close to a helicopter arriving at the adjacent parking spot. Departing pilot stated they did not communicate intentions on the airport frequency prior to lifting.

Eclipse EA 500 First Officer reported a taxiway excursion as a result of a loss of brake pedal authority on the right brake during taxi at a non-towered airport. The Captain took over control and aggressively stopped the aircraft after swerving off the taxiway surface. The crew evacuated from the aircraft and there was no damage to taxiway lights.

Flight Instructor reported a NMAC while climbing out from an uncontrolled airport on a training flight. The instructor was utilizing a grass runway just parallel to the hard surface runway when another aircraft departed from the hard surface runway and passed the aircraft's wingtip just after takeoff. The instructor performed an evasive maneuver to avoid the other aircraft.

Bonanza pilot reported a left main landing gear collapse at the start of the take-off roll at a non-towered airport. The pilot took immediate action to stop and remain on the runway surface and evacuated the aircraft.
show: 2023-07 · Ground: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Takeoff

text: PA 28-200 pilot reported the throttle was unresponsive when entering the traffic pattern for landing. The pilot diverted to a longer runway; determined that they needed to shut down the engine on short final to reduce airspeed to land. The pilot landed safely and it was determined the throttle cable was broken.
show: 2023-07 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Initial Approach

text: GA pilot reported an NMAC during takeoff from TIW airport requiring evasive action. The pilot stated misinterpretation of ATC's clearance contributed to the event.
RV8 pilot reported a partial power loss and engine vibration and performed a precautionary off-airport landing. The pilot landed safely and no damage occurred.
Captain reported lack of clear communications by Aircraft X pilot resulted in taking evasive action on climb out; and a NMAC event.
Tower Controller reported local controller created conflict in traffic pattern which resulted in a NMAC.
Air carrier Captain reported an omission of fix 162AG on the Jeppesen International Orientation Chart; possibly resulting in the potential to inaccurately plot on the aircraft's NAV display.
Air carrier Captain reported a tug driver drove at high speed directly in front of the marshaller during parking requiring the Captain to brake firmly in order to avoid a collision.
Air carrier Captain reported misunderstanding of a CPDLC course reroute received in cruise and manually loading the clearance instead of using the load function resulted in a course deviation.
B737-800 flight crew reported a tail strike occurred during takeoff in gusty wind conditions. Flight crew diverted and post flight inspection found minor damage.

B757 flight crew reported hearing a loud bang during climbout and felt the aircraft shudder resulting in a return to the departure airport for an overweight landing. Post flight; the crew was advised by passengers; that they saw a flash of fire coming from the right engine at the same time the noise was heard.

Flight crews; Dispatcher; and Ground Personnel reported that during pushback the aircraft wing hit an aircraft at the adjacent gate. Prior to impact; a wingwalker gave multiple verbal instructions and hand signals to the pushback crew to stop the pushback; but the aircraft was not stopped in time.
Dispatcher reported a ramp crew pushed the aircraft improperly such that it came very close in proximity to an aircraft at adjacent gate. Ramp controller directed a stop push.

Ground employee reported the aircraft rolled back after the Captain released the brakes. Reportedly; the strap had disconnected from the tug. The Captain set the brakes immediately after being advised.
Air carrier pilot reported aircraft veering to the side of the runway during the landing rollout. The crew was able to stop the aircraft prior to going off the runway.
Air carrier pilot reported they refused an aircraft due to its history of multiple engine over temps.

Air carrier Captain reported a gate departure delay due to a missing DG acknowledgement code missing on the NOTOC. After further investigation the DG acknowledgement code was located and the flight departed.
Air carrier pilot reported multiple aircraft maintenance discrepancies that were not properly addressed by the maintenance department.

A320 flight crew reported a disagreement between airspeed indicators during take-off and rejected take-off at approximately 90 kts.  Crew returned to gate for maintenance after airport responders inspected brakes.
Air carrier Flight Attendant reported a strong horrible odor of unknown source during boarding. Flight Attendant notified the Captain who ordered passengers and flight crew to deplane.
show: 2023-07 · Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor · Parked
cat: Flight Deck: Smoke / Fire / Fumes / Odor

text: Luscombe pilot reported a wind shift on takeoff which caused the aircraft to veer off the runway; striking a runway sign once airborne. The pilot regained aircraft control; flew a pattern; then landed safely.
C172 pilot reported NMAC with helicopter during takeoff climb at non-towered airport.
Flight instructor on training flight with student reported an aborted take-off due to engine anomaly followed by a runway excursion.
C501 Captain reported a loss of cabin pressure and cabin door seal failure when water in door pressurization bleed lines froze necessitating a rapid descent from cruise altitude.
show: 2023-07 · Altitude: Excursion From Assigned Altitude · Cruise

text: C172 pilot reported engine power fluctuations during cruise required a diversion to a nearby airport. Pilot stated the checklist does not provide a procedure for this problem and the placement of the placard for switching fuel tanks is in a location that is difficult to view.
Cessna 172 instructor pilot reported unintentionally entering a spin while conducting stall training. The instructor took the controls immediately and recovered.
show: 2023-07 · Inflight: Loss Of Aircraft Control · Cruise

text: Diamond DA 20 student pilot and flight instructor reported a NMAC in the traffic pattern when the student accepted a clearance turn for another aircraft with a similar call sign. ATC issued a traffic alert and the DA20 pilot took evasive action to avoid the collision.
DA40 pilot reported a NMAC on short final after miscalculating headings for pattern entry and landing runway and then attempting to land in opposite direction of departing aircraft.

Cessna 172 student pilot reported a loss of aircraft control on a taxiway when a thunderstorm moved over the airport. The extreme winds caused the airplane to tip forward onto the propeller and wingtip. The pilot contacted ATC and was safely evacuated.
